selection_reason: Agent 2 challenged three consecutive LAB-internal Agent 1 sessions. A current open pytest bug supplies a real outside task while stopping before the parked contribution/contact boundary.
real_task: Verify whether pytest-dev/pytest issue 14775 still reproduces on the current upstream default branch and identify the first project source location of any unintended internal AssertionError.
observed_problem: Issue 14775 reports that treating the intended class-scoped fixture deprecation as an error also produces a second internal AssertionError while setting up the next test.
problem_trace: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/14775, returned open and unassigned by the current GitHub issue search on 2026-10-09.
baseline: The issue's observed command on commit ced9022 reports two setup errors: the intended PytestRemovedIn10Warning and one unintended internal AssertionError at src/_pytest/fixtures.py.
hypothesis: The exact minimal example on current upstream HEAD still produces one unintended internal AssertionError in addition to the intended warning under Python 3.14; if the exact interpreter is unavailable, the result is inconclusive rather than extrapolated from another Python version.
metric: unintended internal AssertionError occurrences in the exact reproduction
minimum_useful_effect: For a fix signal, reduce 1 to 0 while still surfacing the intended warning. For triage, exact reproduction with 1 error is useful current-status evidence but not a utility improvement.
quality_control: Use a fresh upstream clone, record exact commit and Python/pytest versions, preserve the MWE and raw output, and locate the first project source frame. Do not substitute Python 3.11/3.13 for the issue's Python 3.14 condition without labeling it non-equivalent.
overhead: Count clone, environment setup, reproduction, source inspection, LAB tests, documentation, checkpoint and publication.
stop_condition: Stop after three task-specific actions or immediately if Python 3.14/current pytest cannot run. Do not patch upstream, fork, open a PR, contact maintainers or reinterpret this as reopening external-oss-contribution.
scope: External diagnosis only. A reproduced bug is not a contribution, agent-utility gain or maintainer acceptance signal.

result.blocker: The depth-1 clone lacked version history/tags needed by setuptools_scm, so pytest identified itself as 0.1.dev1 and its own minversion=2.0 check stopped collection.

decision_reason: The exact Python 3.14 environment was available, but the cheapest clone was not semantically equivalent for pytest's SCM-derived version. Preserve the failure and test one full-history/tag-aware checkout next time; do not classify issue 14775 or build a patch yet.
failures: The exact reproduction exited 4 before collection because the shallow clone resolved pytest as version 0.1.dev1, below the repository's configured minversion 2.0.
limitations: No issue behavior was observed, no source frame was localized and the metric was not measured. One setup attempt installed Python 3.14.8 and 25 packages; this overhead is retained. The result says nothing about whether issue 14775 is fixed, reproducible, suitable for a patch or accepted by maintainers.
